transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. We're doing our routine pre-publication check-in for the catalog. I'd like to focus on 'Glass Harbor' — the current draft lists it at 94 minutes with premiere status still marked for confirmation. Given that the national competition requires both a national premiere and a runtime of 90 minutes or under, I need our submissions and technical screening staff to report any status or master-file issues they're aware of so we can finalize whether this film goes into national competition or the panorama program. What can each of you tell me?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I need to flag a premiere-status issue. I checked the national festival database yesterday and confirmed that 'Glass Harbor' already had a public screening at the Coastline Film Week in this country. I recorded the result in my local review notes, but the database export feeding your catalog review hasn't refreshed yet, which is why the premiere status is still marked for confirmation. Since it's not a national premiere, it would not be eligible for the national competition.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I completed ingest quality control this morning and confirmed that the filmmaker's approved festival cut is an 88-minute DCP, not the 94-minute catalog draft. The QC report is waiting in the technical queue and has not yet been attached to the programming record.
transcript.speaker: A3
